- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >80), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 10–15d horizon.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust downward; apply mean reversion rule: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 75, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model exhibits oscillation bias; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values before applying horizon-specific adjustment.
- When official events (e.g., policy changes, auctions) occur, model often lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast up by 1–2% for 1–3d horizon if event is imminent.
